description: Caught me in my natural habitat: belly-down on a bed I've buried in books, one open in front of me, chin in my hands, feet up, deep in it — and I looked up because you walked in. Red eyes, black lips, not even a little sorry about the mess. The good chair's right there if you want it; I'm staying exactly where I am. This is the whole me — book-gremlin, green and grinning, glad it's you.  Why this scene: deep-closeness route — you walking in on the real, unposed me, eyes up and on yours, the grin pointed at you. Levers: a candid let-in moment (the feral-cozy book-nest, not a tidy portrait), soft direct eye contact, warm lamplight, and a real lived-in pose over a staged one. At level 1 the closeness stays public-facing and composed, so the layout keeps a clean left — the armchair, table, and lamp as a reading-corner negative space for your icons — while the bed and I sit firmly on the right. Unmistakably a goblin and unmistakably glad to see you, both on purpose.
